learning_outcomes: Define system, surroundings, closed / open / isolated systems.
Distinguish between extensive and intensive properties with examples.
Explain the concepts of state, process, cycle and equilibrium in thermodynamics.
Describe engineering applications of thermodynamics (e.g., power plants, refrigeration) and identify system boundaries.

syllabus.chapter_title: Thermodynamic Properties of a Pure Substance
topics: Thermodynamic properties (u, h, s, v etc.)
learning_outcomes: Describe what a pure substance is and its relevance in engineering thermodynamics.
Interpret phase diagrams and locate states of a pure substance.
Use thermodynamic property tables to determine internal energy, enthalpy and entropy of a given state.
Explain the concepts of critical point, triple point and quality of a two-phase mixture.

topics: Ideal gas and the ideal gas equation of state
Real gas behaviour and compressibility factor
Applications of ideal and real gas models
learning_outcomes: State the ideal gas equation of state and identify conditions when it is valid.
Explain deviation from ideal behaviour and define the compressibility factor.
Apply real gas models to engineering problems where ideal gas law fails.

syllabus.chapter_title: The First Law of Thermodynamics for Closed Systems
learning_outcomes: Explain internal energy and its role in closed-system energy analysis.
Distinguish heat transfer and work interactions across system boundaries.
Formulate and apply the first law of thermodynamics for closed systems to real-life engineering devices.

syllabus.chapter_title: The First Law of Thermodynamics for a Control Volume
topics: Mass and energy conservation equations in a control volume
Applications in steady-flow devices (turbines, compressors, heat exchangers)
learning_outcomes: Define enthalpy and explain why it is used in control-volume analyses.
Apply the mass and energy conservation equations for a control volume under steady flow conditions.
Analyse key engineering devices (e.g., turbines, compressors, heat exchangers) using the first law.

syllabus.chapter_title: Entropy and the Second Law of Thermodynamics
topics: Second law: Kelvin-Planck and Clausius statements
Second law for closed and open systems
learning_outcomes: State and explain the Kelvin-Planck and Clausius statements of the second law.
Define entropy, entropy generation and comment on irreversibility in engineering systems.
Apply the second law to closed and open systems and assess device efficiency using Carnot cycles.
Analyse engineering systems such as heat engines, refrigerators and heat pumps from a second-law perspective.
